verified_scope: simple unweighted directed and undirected graphs whose influence chain is irreducible, i.e. connected undirected graphs and strongly connected digraphs; reducible input, isolates, edgeless graphs and singletons are refused as NA rather than extended
note: THE SELF-LOOP IS LOAD-BEARING AND THE MEASURE IS NOT COGRAPH'S EXISTING markov. Definition, eqs(9) p1485, (11) p1486 and (20) p1489 with the W construction p1494: set a_ii=1 for every i, W=A/rowSums(A), c=the left eigenvector of W at eigenvalue1 normalised to sum1, Z=(I-W+1c')^-1, M=(I-Z+E Zdg)diag(1/c), and c_IEC(j)=(n-1)/sum_{i!=j} m_ij. M is the Kemeny-Snell mean first passage matrix in the convention m_ij=E[steps from i until j is first reached], so eq(20) sums DOWN column j and the score is a reciprocal mean first passage time INTO j. Page1494 states the construction twice, in the body and in the Table1 note: 'the diagonal entries of its adjacency matrix A=[a_ij] were set to one and its influence network was computed as W=[w_ij]=a_ij/sum_j^n a_ij', following French1956. Footnote10 p1484 gives the reason - 'Given w_ii>0 for any i, all strong networks must be regular', regular meaning aperiodic - and footnote9 p1483 the periodic counterexample. THE LEDGER'S LONG-STANDING ASSUMPTION THAT markov IS IEC UP TO AN N VERSUS N-1 NUMERATOR IS WRONG: markov ALSO omits the self-loop, and that difference is not a rescaling. Computed this session, the largest within-graph spread of iec/markov over the 21 connected five-node graphs is 0.096, and the two rank the nodes differently on 2 of those 21; on the Krackhardt kite iec is 0.069051322 0.069051322 0.052899126 0.103448276 0.052899126 0.099984987 0.099984987 0.055384615 0.018730489 0.010291595 against markov's 0.102457598 0.102457598 0.077345179 0.158102767 0.077345179 0.149691514 0.149691514 0.077669903 0.025856496 0.014270425. markov IS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNCHANGED; iec ships as a separate measure. REDUCIBLE INPUT IS REFUSED, NOT EXTENDED, AND THIS DEPARTS FROM THE BATCH47 PRECEDENT ON PURPOSE: for a reducible W the eigenvalue-one eigenspace has one dimension per closed class so c is undetermined and diag(1/c) undefined, and worse, eq(11) DOES NOT ANNOUNCE THE FAILURE - with Z block diagonal a cross-class pair has z_ij=0 and eq(11) returns the entirely finite m_ij=z_jj/c_j where the true mean first passage time is infinite. Batch47 could apply a reachability mask because ITS source states a zero rule for an unreachable pair; this source states none, and a component-wise reading would additionally have to invent whether the n-1 of eq(20) counts the component or the network. cograph therefore tests irreducibility by boolean closure BEFORE any solve and returns NA at every node with a cograph_undefined_measure warning - never a silent zero and never a finite wrong number. n=1 is NA too, eq(20) dividing by n-1=0; an empty graph returns no scores. An isolate never scores on its own because a graph containing one is reducible. DIRECTION IS KEPT because W is a matrix of directed influence, row i being what actor i attends to, and the measure then needs a STRONGLY connected digraph; there is no in/out/all variant so mode, cutoff and invert_weights are ignored. WEIGHTS ARE DROPPED DELIBERATELY: a_ii=1 is calibrated against a_ij=1, so rescaling the weights would silently re-weight each actor's self-reliance against the network, and the source demonstrates only the binary case. Loops in the input are absorbed by the mandated unit diagonal and parallel edges collapse. normalized=True max-scales, the source stating no normalization. Marked COSTLY: one boolean closure and two dense n x n solves. Zoo2.180 (p104) transcribes the source faithfully, renaming c to v; the sibling labels TEC (eq18) and MEC (eqs21-23) of the same paper are NOT covered. No author or third-party code exists

Zoo 2.221 (comparison-matrix label 'Lhc method', encyclopedia heading 'Lhc index') transcribes the structure of both equations correctly but names the denominator 'Delta, the total number of triangular structures in the network', which read literally is three times too small; on the Krackhardt kite the paper's reading scores node1 at 3305/33=100.15152 where the Zoo's literal wording gives 1380/11=125.45455 (Kendall tau1.0 on that particular graph, but the two are not related by a monotone transform in general). cograph follows the paper; the divergence is reproduced in kite_worked.csv only to show its size. TRIANGLE-FREE GRAPHS ARE AN EXPLICIT COGRAPH DECISION THE SOURCE NEVER MAKES: every tree, star, path, even cycle and bipartite graph has TNTS=0 and TP(u)=0/0 at every node. Because TNTS is a sum of nonnegative counts it vanishes exactly when every numerator NTS(u) vanishes too, so there is no share to distribute and no node with a claim on one; TP is written as ZERO and the index reduces to the pure sum over w in N(v) of sum over u in Phi(w) of k_u/dist(uw)^2, the neighbour-and-location half of the hybrid with the triangle half contributing nothing. definition_source: Liu-Xiong-Shi-Shi-Wang2016 DOI10.1016/j.physa.2016.02.049 PhysicaA452:209-219, 'Evaluating the importance of nodes in complex networks', PII S0378437116002156, CC-BY-NC-ND full open access (the licence line is printed on journal p209 of the PDF itself). THE ORIGINAL FULL TEXT WAS READ. It was retrieved in candidate_review49 with a real browser after every scripted route in candidate_review47 had failed - the block was an Elsevier/Radware BOT WALL, never a licence restriction - and is retained as candidate_review49/dil_liu2016_physa.pdf, SHA256 6964112b658be6c74d409804a125b87e02b0921d895e710863e9fb833cf1422b, 1,757,400 bytes, 11 pages; the hash was RECOMPUTED AND MATCHED THIS SESSION. EVERY EQUATION WAS READ FROM 300dpi PAGE IMAGES RENDERED THIS SESSION, not from the text layer: batch50/png/dil-02.png (journal p210, eq(1) with U, p and lambda, the domain sentence and both Fig.1 worked examples), dil-03.png (p211, eqs(2) and(3), the four printed edge importances, the printed L_v2 and L_v5, and the Fig.2 topology) and dil-09.png (p217, Table3 in full and the Fig.6 ARPA topology). Definition: p = the number of triangles one of whose edges is e_mn, i.e. |N(m) intersect N(n)| in a simple graph; U=(k_m-p-1)(k_n-p-1); lambda=p/2+1; I_emn=U/lambda (1); W_vivj=I_eij*(k_i-1)/(k_i+k_j-2) (2); L_vi=k_i+sum_{vj in Gamma_i} W_vivj (3), Gamma_i the open neighbourhood. THE LAMBDA TRAP IS REAL IN THE ORIGINAL: pdftotext renders the stacked fraction as 'lambda = 2p + 1', and the page image plus the paper's own printed worked example ('p=1, lambda=1/2+1=1.5') both give p/2+1. NO ZOO DIVERGENCE WAS FOUND, which is worth stating because several recent batches did find one: Zoo2.62 transcribes the three equations correctly, and the original agrees SYMBOL FOR SYMBOL with the Almasi-Hu2019 PLoS ONE14(3):e0205936 reproduction (eqs(7)-(9), p10) that candidate_review47 had had to lean on - only the symbol names differ (t->p, C->W, DIL->L). The candidate_review47 caveat that the original had not been read is therefore RETIRED and must not be carried forward. The authors state the domain themselves on p210: 'a network G=(V,E) is an undirected and unweighted network'. They claim O(n<k>^2) complexity, 'Local information', in Table4 p218. THE PAPER PRINTS THREE NUMERICAL FIXTURES, and candidate_review47's 'no published numerical fixture exists' is SUPERSEDED: Fig.1 p210 prints I_e45=9 at p=0 and 8/3 at p=1; Fig.2 p211 prints I_e12=8, I_e227=0, I_e45=2, I_e56=4 and then L_v2=26/9 and L_v5=52/15 on a 27-node tree; and Table3 p217 prints a DIL value for ALL 21 nodes of the ARPA network, whose topology is Fig.6 on the same page. ONE INCONSISTENCY INSIDE THE PAPER IS PRESERVED, NOT FIXED: the prose on p216 calls ARPA 'twenty-one nodes and twenty-three lines', but Table3's own DC column sums to 52, i.e. 26 lines, and Fig.6 draws 26; the DC column and the figure are followed. No author or third-party code exists (the Zoo lists implementations as TBA), so no author-software parity is claimed

THE EDGE LISTS ARE THE WEAK STEP AND ARE CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY BEFORE ANY SCORE IS COMPARED: the 26 ARPA lines read off Fig.6 imply degrees that match Table3's own DC column at ALL 21 nodes, a fatal precondition of the audit, and the Fig.2 reading is pinned by the four printed edge importances. ALL 21 MATCH UNDER ROUNDING, 0 need truncation, 0 match neither; largest |computed-printed| is 3.3333333e-05, entirely the paper's own 4dp printing of 23/3 as 7.6667, 41/12 as 3.4167, 89/15 as 5.9333 and 19/6 as 3.1667. The exact rationals behind the column are 61/4, 287/20, 231/20, 23/3, 23/3, 7, 89/15, 7/2, 7/2, 41/12, 41/12, 13/4, 19/6 x5, 3 x3 and 2, each agreeing with the kernel to <1e-12, and TABLE3'S PRINTED ROW ORDER IS ALSO REPRODUCED as the descending order of the computed values. The ARPA graph contains the triangle (1,2,15), found by exhaustive triple enumeration, so the fixture exercises the p>=1 branch. On the same graph the public wrapper agrees with the kernel to 0 and the NetworkX definitional route to 8.8817842e-16. batch50/run_equivalence.R: 126,967 comparisons carrying 760,577 scalar values, ZERO failures; the 99,304 numerical rows carry 732,914 values at a maximum scaled error of 5.703394e-16 against tolerance 1e-11, and the 27,663 invariant rows record a largest STRUCTURAL residual of 2.728484e-12 (the one larger invariant residual, 0.1666667, is lambda_is_not_2p_plus_1, which records the DISTANCE FROM THE WRONG READING on purpose and is reported apart rather than folded into a headline). ALL 5,532 retained fixtures are inside the domain - the measure has no undefined input - and no score is ever NA or non-finite, checked at 5,532. FOUR REFERENCES, THREE OF WHICH SHARE NO DATA STRUCTURE WITH PRODUCTION: (a) 'exact_sets', EXACT fractions.Fraction ARITHMETIC END TO END WITH NO FLOATING POINT ANYWHERE, the graph held as a dict of PYTHON SETS with p from len(nbr[i] & nbr[j]) and eq(3) accumulated by explicit loops - no numpy, no networkx, no matrix of any kind (5,532 comparisons); (b) 'definitional', NetworkX float64, degrees from G.degree, p from networkx.common_neighbors and eqs(2)-(3) accumulated one incident line at a time in a Python loop over G[i], again with no matrix product (5,532); (c) 'matrix_np', dense float64 NumPy reading p off A@A masked by A - this route DOES share production's matrix-product triangle census and its whole-matrix share expression, is NAMED AS SUCH and is not counted as independent (5,532); (d) 'exact_triples', EXACT Fraction again but with p by EXHAUSTIVE ENUMERATION OF EVERY NODE TRIPLE rather than by set algebra or a matrix power, on the n<=20 part of the collection (5,472). All four take the RAW fixture matrix and do their own projection to the simple undirected skeleton, so a projection bug in production cannot hide. THE PARTS ARE CHECKED SEPARATELY, NOT ONLY THE SCORE: the degree column (5,532), the summed line importance (5,532) and the summed contribution (5,532) against set-based references, plus the full per-edge p, I and W matrices entry by entry on n<=20 (5,472 each). INVARIANTS at 5,532 each: U>=0 on every line, verified independently by checking p<=k-1 at both endpoints; every score at least the node's degree; I symmetric while W is not; and THE CONSERVATION IDENTITY sum_i(L_i-k_i)=sum_e I_e, which follows because the two endpoint shares sum to one and which fails if either the share or the K2 branch is wrong (largest residual 2.728484e-12). COMPONENT LOCALITY IS ASSERTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS on the 5,489 fixtures with n<=30: appending a disjoint triangle-with-pendant leaves every existing score bit-comparable and the appended block scores exactly what it scores alone - DIL is strictly two-hop local, unlike batch48's Lhc. Wrapper, normalized=True, node-permutation, input-projection (weights*13, loops, mode='in', cutoff=1, invert_weights) and an EXPLICIT SYMMETRISATION check each ran at 5,532 comparisons. SEVEN HAND-DERIVED CLOSED FORMS, all independent of every reference route: K_n scores n-1 at every node because p=n-2 makes every U vanish (10 comparisons, n=3..12); a star scores its degree at every node for the same reason, every line touching a leaf (9, m=1..9); a triangle-free k-regular graph scores k+k(k-1)^2/2, so a ring scores 3 and the PETERSEN GRAPH scores 9 (10 + 1); the path P_n scores 1,2.5,3,...,3,2.5,1 (10); and K_{a,b} scores b+b(a-1)(b-1)^2/(a+b-2) on its a-side (5 pairs). THE C_3 BOUNDARY IS ASSERTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, as in batch48: C_3 is K_3, is not triangle-free, and follows the complete-graph form 2 and not the ring form 3. THE K2 0/0 IS TESTED DIRECTLY as an isolated K2, a K2 beside an isolate and two disjoint K2s: every score is finite, never NA, and the kernel's share matrix is a clean zero, so the 0/0 is never evaluated. Degenerate graphs: empty returns no scores, a singleton and an edgeless graph return zeros, and a disconnected graph needs no rule at all. The Krackhardt kite is retained as a named acceptance fixture in kite_worked.csv, every value computed here. 178 public-test expectations passed with ZERO warnings

note: NO ZOO DIVERGENCE AND NO OPEN SOURCE QUESTION - the ORIGINAL WAS READ this session from 300dpi page images (batch50/png/dil-02.png, dil-03.png, dil-09.png) of the CC-BY-NC-ND PDF retained in candidate_review49, hash rematched. Definition, eqs(1)-(3) journal pp210-211: p=|N(i) intersect N(j)| is the number of triangles on the line, U=(k_i-p-1)(k_j-p-1), lambda=p/2+1, I_eij=U/lambda, W_vivj=I_eij*(k_i-1)/(k_i+k_j-2), L_vi=k_i+sum over the open neighbourhood of W. LAMBDA IS p/2+1: pdftotext renders that stacked fraction as '2p+1' IN THE ORIGINAL AS WELL AS IN THE ALMASI-HU REPRODUCTION, and the page image and the paper's own printed example ('p=1, lambda=1/2+1=1.5', I_e45=8/3) both settle it. Zoo2.62 and Almasi-Hu2019 eqs(7)-(9) agree with the original symbol for symbol; candidate_review47's 'original not read' caveat is RETIRED. DIRECTION AND WEIGHTS ARE PROJECTED AWAY, NOT REFUSED, because the authors state the domain themselves on p210 - 'an undirected and unweighted network' - and every quantity in the three equations is a count. A directed, weighted or multigraph input is symmetrised, its weights and parallel lines collapsed and its loops dropped, SILENTLY, which is the convention every other undirected-domain measure in centrality() already follows; warning on each would be noisy and inconsistent with its twenty-odd siblings, and the projection is documented on the help page and asserted in the tests. No in/out/all reading exists, so the measure is in the no-mode family and cutoff and invert_weights are ignored. NOT MARKED COSTLY: the source claims O(n<k>^2) 'Local information' in Table4 p218 and the kernel is one masked matrix product plus elementwise work, so it stays in type='all'. THE ISOLATED K2 IS THE ONE 0/0 AND IT IS RESOLVED, NOT REFUSED, WHICH IS A DELIBERATE DEPARTURE FROM BATCH49: k_i+k_j-2 vanishes only when both endpoints have degree one, since every endpoint of a line has degree at least one, and there p=0 and U=(1-0-1)(1-0-1)=0 as well, so the importance being split is EXACTLY ZERO while the split of it is 0/0. Because W is a SHARE of I and the two shares sum to one wherever defined, every admissible split of an exactly zero importance gives an exactly zero contribution - the answer does not depend on resolving the indeterminacy - so the share is written as zero WITH THE TEST TAKEN BEFORE THE DIVISION and both K2 nodes score 1. THE SOURCE SAYS NOTHING ABOUT THIS CASE (grepped for denominator/zero/undefined); the choice is cograph's and it follows the batch48 lhc precedent, where TNTS=0 makes TP a 0/0 on every triangle-free graph and is likewise written as zero because the denominator vanishes exactly where every numerator does. It deliberately does NOT follow batch49 iec, which returns NA on reducible input: there the closed form returns a FINITE WRONG NUMBER where the truth is infinite, so a value would be wrong; here every candidate value is the same value. Isolates, singletons, edgeless and disconnected input need no rule - an isolate has an empty sum and scores 0, and raw scores are component-local because nothing reaches past a node's second neighbours. normalized=True max-scales, the source stating no normalization. U>=0 always, since p<=k_i-1, so no score falls below its node's degree. AN INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY IN THE PAPER IS PRESERVED: p216 says the ARPA network has 23 lines where Table3's DC column sums to 52 (26 lines) and Fig.6 draws 26; the DC column and the figure are followed and the edge list is NOT trimmed

definition_source: Sheng-Zhu-Wang-Wang-Hou2020 DOI10.3390/a13110280 Algorithms13(11):280, 'Identifying Influential Nodes of Complex Networks Based on Trust-Value', MDPI CC BY, FULLY OPEN ACCESS, 15pp; eqs(2) and(4) journal p5, eqs(5) and(6) p5, eq(7) and Algorithm1 p7, Figure3 and Table3 p6, Table4 p8, section3.3 p9, Figure5 and Table5 p10. THE ORIGINAL WAS READ AND ITS PDF HASH RECOMPUTED AND MATCHED THIS SESSION (candidate_review48/tpr_sheng2020_algorithms.pdf, SHA256 0b1fdd201fee74c33191fe548f8aa0d9ae05a86f73736a90e8f9c39db6354541); pages5, 6, 7 and10 were rendered to 200dpi as batch51/png/sheng-05.png, -06, -07, -10 and ALL FOUR VISUALLY INSPECTED, plus a 500dpi crop of Figure5(a) for the kite's node labelling. THE ZOO MIS-CITES THIS MEASURE: Zoo2.381 reference[350] is Sheng et al2020 PhysicaA541:123262 doi10.1016/j.physa.2019.123262, the 'global and local structure' paper, which is Zoo2.149 and a DIFFERENT MEASURE; a reader following the Zoo's reference lands on the wrong paper. The Zoo's own 2.381 formulas are eqs(2), (5), (6) and(7) of the Algorithms paper verbatim, but it OMITS the s(a,a)=1 base case of eq(4) and says nothing about the recursion's domain, and both are load-bearing. Access note, reusable for any MDPI paper: mdpi.com/<journal>/<vol>/<iss>/<art>/pdf returns 403 to a non-browser client, res.mdpi.com/d_attachment/... returns 200. Definition: Rs(i,j)=s(i,j)/sum_{k in N_j} s(j,k) (2); s(a,b)=1 if a=b else (C/(|Na||Nb|)) sum_{l in Na} sum_{m in Nb} s(l,m) (4); Rd(i,j)=d_i/sum_{k in N_j} d_k (5); T(i,j)=(1-k)Rs+k Rd (6); TPR_i^t=(1-alpha)/n+alpha sum_{j in N_i} T(i,j) TPR_j^{t-1} (7). Defaults from the paper: C=1 (p5), alpha=0.85 (below eq7 p7), k=0.85 with domain [0,1] (below eq6 p5; section3.3 p9 picks it from a Kendall-against-SIR sweep peaking between0.85 and0.9 on PolBooks). FIGURE3 p6, READ FROM THE PAGE IMAGE, annotates the two arcs between nodes1 and2 with (1-k)x0.6/1.11+k x3/7 and (1-k)x0.6/1.59+k x2/9, and EVERY SYMBOL RESOLVES against a quantity computed here - 0.6=s(1,2), 1.11=S_2, 3=d_1, 7=D_2, 1.59=S_1, 2=d_2, 9=D_1 - which instantiates eqs(2) and(5) and FIXES THE (1-k)-ON-SIMILARITY ORIENTATION of eq(6). That matters because the independent restatement, Hajarathaiah-Enduri-Anamalamudi-SubbaReddy-Tokala2022 DOI10.3390/e24050704 Entropy24(5):704 (also obtained and read, SHA256 0990e7c1f0eddfc1fa62b3aa778758deada00a2174504296914a3758b906900b), prints a TV matrix that is 0.85 SR+0.15 DR while its own equation says (1-k)SR+k DR; Sheng's Figure3 settles it in favour of the equation as printed. THE PRIOR BLOCKER FROM candidate_review40 IS CLOSED AND IT WAS NEVER AN ITERATION COUNT: Algorithm1 line4, read from the page image, is 'for CONNECTED node v_u, v_v in V do' and Table3's caption says 'the short dash indicates that there is no edge between the two nodes', so the similarity map holds only adjacent pairs plus the diagonal and A NON-ADJACENT PAIR CONTRIBUTES 0, not0.1. Under that domain the diagonal is the only inhomogeneous term, it reaches a line exactly through the triangles that line carries, every row sum of the linear part is at most 1-p/(d_a d_b), and the recursion CONTRACTS on any block carrying a triangle even at C=1 (measured spectral radii this session: K3 0.750, K4 0.778, K5 0.813, bull0.742, kite0.681, karate0.575, house0.784, Sheng Fig3 0.719; exactly1.000000 on K2, P3, star, C4 and K3,3, all triangle-free). TWO SETS OF NUMBERS IN THE candidate_review48 AUDIT ARE THE REJECTED READING'S, AND THE CAUSE IS IDENTIFIED RATHER THAN MERELY REPORTED: its Table3 sweep deviations (0.350, 0.240, 0.162, 0.067, 0.042 at 1/2/3/5/10 sweeps) and its kite TPR magnitudes (7:0.18800388 ...) are BOTH the REJECTED non-adjacent-0.1 reading's, not the accepted reading it advocates - recomputed here the accepted reading gives 0.350, 0.252, 0.182, 0.097, 0.022 and 7:0.1883952454, while the pinned reading reproduces its printed lists EXACTLY, all five sweeps and all seven kite values; its own retained trust-pagerank_worked.csv holds the accepted values, so its prose and its fixture disagreed; its '|delta| = 1.4e-17' for the kite's automorphism-forced ties is also not what is measured here, two of the three pairs being EXACTLY equal in double precision. None of it changes a conclusion - the verdict, the domain finding and the ranking claims all stand - but every number was caught only by recomputing, and nothing from either prior audit entered the implementation unrecomputed. published_audit.R computes both sweep lists and ASSERTS the pinned one reproduces the audit's printed list. THE SOURCE'S CLAIM THAT C DOES NOT MATTER IS FALSE FOR THE CONVERGED RECURSION: it holds for a homogeneous recursion where C is an overall scale that cancels in the ratio, but the diagonal makes this one affine so C enters the resolvent (I-CM)^-1 too; measured on the karate club, C from1 to0.5 moves Rs by up to0.141 and the scores by up to9.074920e-4, and at C=0.05 the Rs shift reaches0.310, while the karate top five is unmoved - defensible about rankings, wrong about results. tpr_decay is therefore exposed, defaulting to the source's1. No author or third-party code exists and no CRAN or NetworkX implementation of TPR was found, so NO AUTHOR-SOFTWARE PARITY IS CLAIMED; the paper's SIR spreading experiments and Figures6-8 were not reproduced
